content.text: Contributors: Melissa Bialowas, Rayna CummingsAuthorInstructorInstructor: Rayna Cummings Show more Natural Numbers Natural numbers are any positive whole numbers used for counting things. For example, the numbers 1 to 20 are natural numbers because they are all used in counting and have a positive sign. However, fractions, decimals, and negative numbers are not included in this category. Numbers like 1/3 and 4.20 are not natural numbers because they are in fraction form and are not whole numbers. Natural numbers are commonly used in day-to-day counting but may vary their definition depending on the context. Is Zero a Natural Number? Zero (0) as a natural number is a subject of debate. In traditional counting, people start counting from one, which excludes the number zero from the set of natural numbers. In some areas of mathematics, like set theory, zero is considered part of the natural numbers. Zero as a Neutral Integer Zero has a unique state, it is not positive or negative. It is classified as a real number, a whole number, and an integer. Consider the number line: you can find that zero is positioned at the center (origin) between the positive and negative numbers. For this reason, it can be said that zero is a neutral integer. Zero's Status in Mathematics Some mathematicians agree that if it is not negative and a whole number, then it can be included in the set of natural numbers. On the other hand, some disagree because it represents "nothing" and cannot be used in counting objects. The difference in the definition of zero depends on what mathematical domain it is being used. Zero plays a very important role in different branches of mathematics, its definition as a natural number still depends on the context, interpretation, and its application.
